records.name: Trump Turnberry Resort
records.description: Legendary Ayrshire golf resort on the coast, home to the Open Championship-hosting Ailsa Course and wide sea views toward Ailsa Craig.

records.name: Ailsa Course
records.description: Famous championship links course repeatedly used for the Open, known for cliff-top holes and dramatic lighthouse views.

records.name: Turnberry Lighthouse
records.description: Turnberry Lighthouse, or Turnberry Point Lighthouse, is a category B listed minor light on the South Ayrshire coast of Scotland. It was designed by David and Thomas Stevenson and completed in 1873. It is a conspicuous landmark when seen from the Ayrshire Coastal Path and the Trump Turnberry golf resort.

records.name: Ailsa Craig Viewpoint
records.description: Classic coastal viewpoint toward the volcanic island of Ailsa Craig, a striking constant on the horizon from Turnberry's shoreline.

records.name: Culzean Castle
records.description: Culzean Castle is a castle overlooking the Firth of Clyde, near Maybole, Carrick, in South Ayrshire, on the west coast of Scotland. It is the former home of the Marquess of Ailsa, the chief of Clan Kennedy, but is now owned by the National Trust for Scotland. The clifftop castle lies within the 240 acres (97 ha) Culzean Castle Country Park, which also contains a walled garden, other estate buildings that are open to the public, shops and cafés, and a playground. The castle is open to the public throughout the summer, and the wider estate is open all year.

records.name: Culzean Country Park
records.description: Extensive clifftop estate grounds surrounding Culzean Castle with formal gardens, woodland walks and sea panoramas.

records.name: Electric Brae
records.description: The Electric Brae is a gravity hill in South Ayrshire, Scotland, where a freewheeling vehicle will appear to be drawn uphill by some mysterious attraction. The phenomenon is an optical illusion.

records.name: Dunure Castle
records.description: Dunure Castle is located on the west coast of Scotland, in South Ayrshire, about five miles south of Ayr and close to the village of Dunure. Today the castle stands in ruins on a rocky promontory on the Carrick coast, overlooking the small harbour of Dunure.

records.name: Crossraguel Abbey
records.description: The Abbey of Saint Mary of Crossraguel is a ruin of a former Cluniac abbey near the town of Maybole, South Ayrshire, Scotland. Although it is a ruin, visitors can still see the monks’ church, cloister and dovecote.

records.name: Kennedy's Castle
records.description: Ruined clifftop stronghold traditionally linked with the Kennedy family and dramatic views over the Ayrshire coast.

records.name: Maybole Castle
records.description: Maybole Castle is a 16th-century castle located on High Street in Maybole, South Ayrshire, Scotland. Originally built for the Earls of Cassillis, it is an L-shaped construction with Victorian two-storey extensions. It is associated with a legend of John Faa, in which an earl killed Faa and imprisoned his wife, the Countess of Cassillis, in the castle.

records.name: Maidens Harbour
records.description: Pretty harbour village south of Culzean and Turnberry, good for coastal views and short promenade walks.

records.name: Culzean Beach
records.description: Beautiful estate beach below the castle cliffs, reached by scenic paths through the Culzean grounds.

records.name: Culzean Swan Pond
records.description: Pretty ornamental water feature within the estate, surrounded by formal parkland and family paths.

records.name: Culzean Deer Park
records.description: Wooded and open estate area where wildlife, long drives and big sea views define the Culzean experience.

records.name: Eisenhower Apartment
records.description: The famous apartment gifted to General Eisenhower inside the castle, adding wartime interest to the estate.

records.name: Culzean Walled Garden
records.description: Formal garden space within the estate, rewarding visitors who want more than the headline castle view.

records.name: Caves of Culzean
records.description: Sea caves beneath the estate cliffs that add geological drama to beach walks under the castle.

records.name: Maidens Beach
records.description: Small coastal beach near the harbour village, with lovely views north toward Culzean.

records.name: Croy Shore
records.description: Rocky coastal strip near Electric Brae, valued for its sense of open sea and uncluttered shoreline.

records.name: Turnberry Beach
records.description: Broad sweep of shore below the famous links and lighthouse, with excellent Ailsa Craig views.

records.name: Turnberry Point
records.description: Headland viewpoint where golf, cliffs, lighthouse and the sea come together in classic Ayrshire style.

records.name: Souter Johnnie's Cottage
records.description: Thatched cottage in Kirkoswald linked to Tam o' Shanter and a popular literary heritage detour.

records.name: Bachelors' Club Tarbolton
records.description: National Trust property associated with Robert Burns and one of the most evocative literary sites in Ayrshire.

records.name: Kirkoswald Village
records.description: Pleasant village rich in Burns connections and traditional South Ayrshire character.

records.name: Kirkoswald Old Kirk
records.description: Atmospheric ruined kirk and graveyard that suit a slow heritage stop on the road to Turnberry.

records.name: Kennedy's Pass
records.description: Clifftop viewpoint in the Carrick coast area with a dramatic sense of the shoreline's rugged character.

records.name: Ballochmyle Viaduct
records.description: Remarkable railway viaduct over the River Ayr, included here as a classic Ayrshire engineering detour.

records.name: Carrick Hills Viewpoint
records.description: High rural viewpoint above the Carrick plain, good for understanding Turnberry's wider landscape setting.

records.name: Ailsa Craig Boat View
records.description: Classic sea view location for Scotland's volcanic island landmark, especially striking in clear evening light.

records.name: Dunure Harbour
records.description: Small stone harbour full of character, sitting just below one of Ayrshire's finest castle ruins.

records.name: Bargany Gardens
records.description: Renowned private gardens in the Girvan district, especially celebrated for seasonal displays and mature plantings.

records.name: Glenapp Castle Viewpoint
records.description: Viewpoint area toward the grand castle hotel estate and the wilder southern end of the Ayrshire coast.

records.name: Pinwherry Castle
records.description: Ruined tower-house in a quiet rural setting south of Girvan, echoing the feudal history of Carrick.

records.name: Lendalfoot Beach
records.description: Open stretch of shingle and sand on the coast south of Turnberry, framed by dramatic headlands.

records.name: Bennane Head
records.description: Dramatic coastal viewpoint on the route south, known for cliffs, sea stacks and stormy-weather scenery.

records.name: Culzean Home Farm
records.description: Part of the wider estate story, recalling the practical working landscape behind the castle's grandeur.

records.name: Maybole Collegiate Church
records.description: Historic church site reflecting Maybole's importance as the old capital of Carrick.

records.name: Brown Carrick Hill
records.description: Excellent hill walk and viewpoint above the Ayrshire coast, offering a wider panorama over Turnberry country.

records.name: Turnberry Golf Academy
records.description: Practice and coaching facility that complements the resort's championship courses and golfing reputation.
